exposure: Fetal indications (neurological abnormalities, aneuploidy or genetic syndromes, cardiac malformations, structural malformations, genetic abnormalities)
outcome: Time between referral and maternal-fetal medicine review
Time between maternal-fetal medicine review and feticide
cohort: The study included singleton pregnancies undergoing feticide at 22 weeks' gestation or later at the Centre for Advanced Prenatal Care at the Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital, a tertiary perinatal centre, between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2020.
finding: Most late pregnancy feticides were performed due to fetal indications, primarily structural malformations or genetic abnormalities, and the annual number of feticides increased from 20 to 54 over the decade while the median gestational age at feticide remained consistent.
